data.summary: The plan front‑loads the student’s weak units (Kinetics and Equilibrium) while still covering the core curriculum. Each week balances lecture topics, live class participation, and focused practice within a 6‑hour limit. The final two weeks are reserved for mixed review and timed free‑response practice to build stamina for the exam.

weeks.focus: Introduce foundational concepts and begin Kinetics basics.
tasks: Read AP Chemistry textbook sections on Moles and Molar Mass and Atomic Structure; take notes on key formulas.
Watch a 20‑minute video on Reaction Rates and write a one‑page summary.
Do 8 practice problems on calculating reaction rates (5.1) and check answers with the solution guide.
Complete 5 free‑response style questions on rate law basics (5.2) and self‑grade using the AP scoring rubric.

weeks.focus: Live class on Kinetics; reinforce rate law concepts.
tasks: Attend live class 9000 and actively take notes on examples presented.
After class, redo the class’s example problems without notes to test retention.
Complete 10 additional rate‑law FRQs, marking each against the scoring guide.
Create a one‑page cheat sheet summarizing the steps to determine a rate law from experimental data.

weeks.focus: Complete Kinetics unit and start Thermochemistry.
tasks: Read sections on Concentration Changes Over Time and Elementary Reactions; outline key equations.
Solve 6 problems on concentration vs. time graphs (5.3).
Watch a tutorial on Energy Diagrams and label endothermic vs. exothermic curves.
Do 5 calorimetry calculations (6.1, 6.2) and verify with answer key.

weeks.focus: Live class on Equilibrium; introduce equilibrium concepts.
tasks: Attend live class 9001, focusing on the derivation of the reaction quotient.
After class, write out the steps to determine direction of a reversible reaction for 4 different examples.
Complete 8 practice problems calculating Q and comparing to K (7.3).
Summarize the three equilibrium principles on a one‑page mind map.

weeks.focus: Finish Equilibrium unit and begin Acids & Bases.
tasks: Read textbook sections on Calculating the Equilibrium Constant; solve 6 problems (7.4).
Watch a video on Acid‑Base introductions; list the definitions of acids and bases.
Do 10 pH calculations for strong acids and bases (8.2).
Create a table converting between pH, pOH, [H+], and [OH-] for quick reference.

weeks.focus: Deepen Acids & Bases; start Thermodynamics & Electrochemistry.
tasks: Solve 8 weak‑acid equilibrium problems (8.3) using ICE tables.
Write a short explanation of buffer action and solve 4 buffer‑preparation problems (8.4).
Read sections on Entropy; complete 5 conceptual questions (9.1).
Calculate entropy changes for 3 reactions (9.2) and check work with solution set.

weeks.focus: Live class on Acids & Bases; practice strong‑acid/base calculations.
tasks: Attend live class 9002 and note any alternative methods shown for pH calculations.
Redo the class examples without notes to ensure mastery.
Complete 12 mixed strong‑acid/base FRQs, grading with the AP rubric.
Update the pH/pOH reference table with any new shortcuts learned.

weeks.focus: Complete Thermodynamics & Electrochemistry; review all units briefly.
tasks: Work through 6 Gibbs free‑energy problems (9.3) and interpret spontaneity.
Solve 5 cell‑potential calculations for galvanic and electrolytic cells (9.4).
Do 4 stoichiometry word problems that involve gases (4.5, 3.4).
Create a one‑page summary linking ΔG, K, and equilibrium concepts.

weeks.focus: Mixed review of all units; timed free‑response practice.
tasks: Set a 90‑minute timer and complete 3 full‑length AP free‑response questions covering different units.
Review answers using the scoring guide; note any recurring mistakes.
Do a quick‑fire round: 15 multiple‑choice questions (one from each listed topic).
Update a personal error‑log with strategies to avoid those mistakes.

weeks.focus: Final comprehensive review and exam‑day strategy.
tasks: Take a full 90‑minute practice exam under timed conditions.
Score the exam, then spend 2 hours reviewing every incorrect answer with the rubric.
Re‑read the one‑page cheat sheets created earlier for each major unit.
Write a brief exam‑day checklist (materials, timing plan, stress‑relief techniques).

data.final_week_advice: Stay calm, trust your preparation, and use the checklist to manage time on exam day. Review your error‑log quickly before the test, and remember to pace yourself—answer every free‑response prompt even if you’re unsure, and allocate a minute per multiple‑choice question.
